---
title: "Query a large CSV file lazily"
---

Filter and aggregate a CSV file with a lazy query, so that Polars can push the column selection and the filter into the CSV reader.

Requires the phpolars extension ([Getting started](../getting-started.qmd)). Runnable scripts: [lazy-csv.setup.php](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phpstats/phpolars/main/docs/examples/lazy-csv.setup.php) and [lazy-csv.php](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phpstats/phpolars/main/docs/examples/lazy-csv.php).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Make the input file

The setup script writes `orders.csv`, one million orders in six columns (53 MB), to the current directory. It stops if the file already exists.

{{< include _lazy-csv.setup.md >}}
:::

{{< include _lazy-csv.md >}}

- `PROJECT 3/6 COLUMNS`: the reader converts only three columns to values. It still reads and splits every line of the file.
- `SELECTION`: the filter runs during the scan, so rejected rows never reach the aggregation.
- `ESTIMATED ROWS` is the planner's estimate, not a count.
- `scan_csv()` doesn't open the file. A missing file raises an error at `explain()` or `collect()`.
- `read_csv()` would parse all six columns of every row before filtering.
- `collect(engine: 'streaming')` runs the query in batches. On a 276 MB version of this file, it peaked at 71 MB, against 217 MB with the default engine (one run each, macOS).

Reference: [scan_csv()](../reference/io.qmd#fn-scan_csv) · [explain()](../reference/dataframe.qmd#lazyframe-explain) · [collect()](../reference/dataframe.qmd#lazyframe-collect) · [Lazy queries](../getting-started.qmd#lazy-queries) · [Memory on large files](../performance.qmd#memory-on-large-files)
